stories.headline: Ganjam on high alert amid 3rd cyclone alert
stories.title: Ganjam on high alert amid 3rd cyclone alert
stories.summary: The Collector instructed field-level officials to inspect all cyclone shelters and ensure the availability of drinking water, food, electricity, lighting and sanitation facilities.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

Brahmapur: With Ganjam district facing the possibility of a cyclone accompanied by heavy rainfall and strong winds on November 18 and 19, the district administration has sounded a high alert and initiated extensive precautionary measures, setting a zero-casualty target to safeguard lives, livestock and property.

A high-level preparedness meeting of departmental officials was held at Chhatrapur on Saturday under the chairmanship of Collector V Keerthi Vasan, who directed all departments to remain on alert and ensure coordinated action to meet any eventuality.
Drawing lessons from the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods, he stressed the need for advance preparedness rather than a last-minute response.
The Fisheries Department has been directed to ensure that all fishermen currently out at sea return to the shore by November 16.
Fishing activities will remain prohibited thereafter.
A public awareness campaign through loudspeakers will begin in all blocks from Sunday to sensitise people about the impending weather threat.
The BDOs will coordinate with elected representatives, Self-Help Groups and local communities to disseminate warnings and safety advisories.
Vulnerable people will be shifted to safer locations whenever necessary.
Pregnant women will be identified and moved to safer places in advance through coordinated efforts of the Health and Social Welfare departments.
Special arrangements have also been made for livestock protection.

Health centres will be stocked with essential medicines, including anti-snake venom injections, while the Animal Resources Development Department will make arrangements for the safe accommodation of cattle and other domestic animals.

stories.headline: FPI buying hits 5-year high in November. What's driving the $7.5 billion inflow?
stories.title: FPI buying hits 5-year high in November. What's driving the $7.5 billion inflow?
stories.summary: Mumbai: In a sharp U-turn after months of sustained selling, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) pumped $7.5 billion into Indian equities in the first 10 trading sessions of November - the highest monthly inflow in five years, according to Bloomberg data.This comes after FPIs withdrew $2.17 billion from Indian equities in October and $3.46 billion in September. The net investments in November so far are the highest since November 2021. The last time foreign investors pumped in more money in a single month was November 2020, when inflows stood at $9.56 billion, the data showed.135868866According to fund managers, FPIs have been aggressively investing amid a correction in AI-related stocks globally and a decline in crude oil prices. "The FPI flows are driven by multiple factors. profit booking on AI Investments, drop in oil prices, election results in Brazil, correction in Indian valuations over last two years, talks of exemptions on capital gains and reduction in rupee volatility," said Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra AMC.All this came in quick succession and the combined effect is visible in FPI flows, he said.Read more: IPO calendar: Mahanadi Coalfields among 3 companies to raise over Rs 10,000 cr in busy week for primary marketBrent crude prices have fallen nearly 21% to $93.37 per barrel on November 13 from a peak of $118 on October 30. The Indian rupee has appreciated by ₹1.97, or about 2%, against the US dollar since the beginning of October, rising from ₹96.22 per dollar to ₹94.25 per dollar by mid-November.Domestic institutional investors, meanwhile, have turned net sellers, booking profits amid a sharp rally in the market, after providing a crucial backstop through much of the year. DIIs have sold equities worth over ₹49,000 crore in the first 10 trading sessions of November, according to NSE data. Since the beginning of November, the Sensex and Nifty have gained nearly 10% each, while the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices have advanced around 8% each.Read more: Will Sensex, Nifty continue their bull run or consolidate? 4 factors to watch out for this weekOverseas investors began 2026 with net outflows of $3.26 billion into Indian equities in January, before turning net buyers in February with investments of $1.69 billion. However, the respite was short-lived, as March saw a sharp reversal, with FPIs pulling out $13.23 billion - their biggest monthly sell-off.Their return to Indian equities reflects both global portfolio rotation away from AI-heavy markets and improving outlook for India, said Anurag Byas, director for global markets solutions at Rothschild & Co. "Lower crude prices, better earnings and now attractive valuations seem to have supported this sentiment change. This is a positive signal but may be early to be extrapolated; the fundamentals must improve and the oil and currency stability must hold for this to become a sustained trend," he said. Shah of Kotak Mahindra AMC expects FPI flows to move in line with how the above factors interplay with each other.

profit booking on AI Investments, drop in oil prices, election results in Brazil, correction in Indian valuations over last two years, talks of exemptions on capital gains and reduction in rupee volatility," said Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra AMC.

Domestic institutional investors, meanwhile, have turned net sellers, booking profits amid a sharp rally in the market, after providing a crucial backstop through much of the year.

This is a positive signal but may be early to be extrapolated; the fundamentals must improve and the oil and currency stability must hold for this to become a sustained trend," he said.
